So Texas seems to be a bit of a special case. Apparently "if you are familiar with Texas’ mechanics lien laws you know that they are the most confusing and convoluted in all of the world". Generally speaking, your general contractor should have signed, and have his subcontractors sign a contract that includes a "No Lien Clause". Texas has amended some laws in 2013 to make this waiver not apply in many commercial instances. "Texas has recently enacted laws that change what lien rights can and cannot be waived."

But then says they are still fully enforceable for residential construction on single-family dwellings. "The new statutory lien waiver forms are generally not required in order to waive a lien in a contract for residential construction if the contract was made before labor or materials are provided. Therefore, a residential or residential development contract may still contain a blanket waiver if signed before the work starts"

If you plan on doing future work, you should check out http://www.zlien.com/lien-waivers/texas-lien-waiver-faqs/

Apparently you can print the actual form Texas now requires from https://app.zlien.com/waiver_exchange/?q=TWlzc2luZyBQYXJhbWV0ZXJz&error=1
